newsitem.title: USA: NY voters back green bond by 3 to 1 margin - poll.
newsitem.headline: NY voters back green bond by 3 to 1 margin - poll.

text.p: New York State voters, who in 1990 rejected former Gov. Mario Cuomo's proposal for a green bond, will probably approve on Nov 5 a similar $1.75 billion bond pushed by the Pataki Administration, a poll said Sunday.

By a 56 to 41 percent margin, state voters said they are willing to pay higher taxes to clean up the state's air, land and waters, while 73 percent of them agreed pollution was a "big problem" in New York.

"They approve of the proposed environmental bond issue -- Gov. (George) Pataki's pet project and the big question on the state ballot," said Maurice Carroll, director of the Quinnipiac College Poling Institute, in prepared remarks.
The survey of 705 New Yorkers was conducted Sept 11 to 17 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.7 percent.
Gov. Pataki has campaigned vigorously for the environmental bond act, and the survey specualted that his approval ratings rose to the highest level he has enjoyed in in part due to this effort.
Pataki's overall approval rating reached 51 to 35 percent, the survey said, adding another possible reasons for the rise could be Pataki's speech in August at the Republican convention in San Diego.
